title: Building Effective Agents
summary: Anthropic's practical framework for agent design: five composable workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer), and clear guidance on when a workflow beats a full agent.

title: Agent Development Kit (ADK) documentation
summary: Google's open-source, code-first toolkit (Python/Java/Go/TypeScript) for building, evaluating, and deploying multi-agent applications; model-agnostic but optimized for Gemini.

title: Agent Development Kit: making it easy to build multi-agent applications
summary: Google Developers Blog announcement introducing ADK, its design goals, and how Agent/Workflow classes compose into multi-agent systems.

title: LangGraph overview
summary: LangChain's low-level orchestration framework for long-running, stateful agents, modeled as graphs of shared state, nodes, and edges.

title: CrewAI — Introduction
summary: Role-based multi-agent orchestration framework: Crews (collaborative agents with roles/goals) combined with Flows (precise, event-driven control).

title: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
summary: The open standard ("USB-C for AI") that lets agents connect to external tools, data sources, and workflows through a common client/server protocol.

title: Introducing the Model Context Protocol
summary: Anthropic's original announcement of MCP and the problem it solves: standardizing how applications provide context to LLMs and agents.

title: Prompting best practices
summary: The living reference for prompt engineering with Claude: clarity, examples, XML structuring, chain-of-thought, and agentic prompting techniques.

title: Introduction to Large Language Models
summary: Google's free crash-course module on LLM fundamentals: tokens, n-grams, Transformers, self-attention, fine-tuning, and known failure modes.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (Lewis et al., 2020)
summary: The original RAG paper: a generator model conditioned on passages fetched by a learned retriever, beating purely parametric models on open-domain QA. arXiv:2005.11401.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) — Pinecone Learning Center
summary: Practical explainer of the RAG architecture pattern: retriever + vector database + generator, and why it reduces hallucination versus pure parametric recall.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation — Pinecone learning series
summary: A multi-part series covering advanced RAG techniques: two-stage retrieval with reranking, hybrid search, multi-query retrieval.

title: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
summary: The paper that introduced the Transformer architecture, based entirely on attention and dropping recurrence/convolution — the foundation every modern LLM is built on. arXiv:1706.03762.

title: The Illustrated Transformer
summary: Jay Alammar's diagram-led walkthrough of self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding, and the encoder/decoder stack — the standard first read for understanding how Transformers actually work.

title: Hugging Face LLM Course
summary: Free, hands-on course on the Hugging Face ecosystem (Transformers, Datasets, Tokenizers): how Transformer models work, fine-tuning, and sharing results on the Hub.

title: CS224N: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning
summary: Stanford's graduate NLP course: word vectors, neural network models for language, and the latest LLM research, with public lecture videos and assignments.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation (short course)
summary: DeepLearning.AI short course covering basic to advanced (agentic) RAG techniques, with hands-on notebooks.

title: AI Agents in LangGraph (short course)
summary: DeepLearning.AI short course, taught with LangChain's founder, on building single- and multi-agent LLM applications with LangGraph.

title: Get text embeddings
summary: Vertex AI reference for generating text embeddings via the API/SDK, including available embedding models and output vector dimensions.

title: Choose an embeddings task type
summary: How to pick RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT vs RETRIEVAL_QUERY vs SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY task types so Gemini's embedding model optimizes the vector space for your use case.

title: Vector Search overview
summary: Vertex AI's fully-managed vector database built on the ScaNN approximate-nearest-neighbor algorithm, for semantic search and recommendations at scale.

title: Vertex AI APIs for building search and RAG experiences
summary: The Agent Search/App Builder APIs for building enterprise search and RAG applications on top of your own data stores.

title: About apps and data stores
summary: How Gemini Enterprise's data stores and connectors (SharePoint, Jira, Confluence, ServiceNow, etc.) ingest or federate company data for grounded search.

title: Grounding with Agent Search
summary: How to ground Gemini responses in a Vertex AI Search data store so enterprise answers come with citations back to source documents.
